product: Speechmatics — speech to text, Realtime (WebSocket v2)

source_audio.description: No audio was submitted and no request was issued: this frame is authored to Speechmatics' published Realtime protocol documentation, not captured from the service. The RecognitionStarted message carries no transcript, so no spoken or written content is involved at all.

redaction.notes: Nothing was redacted because nothing was captured. The session id holds the nil GUID — the placeholder form protocol section 4 prescribes for a correlating identifier — because no real session exists to name, and the orchestrator version is deliberately a fixture label rather than a real Speechmatics build number.

terms.basis: docs/guides/provider-recording-protocol.md section 7 — no Output was captured at all; the fixture is authored to Speechmatics' published protocol documentation. Speechmatics STT's own verdict for a capture is permitted, and it is not what blocks one here (see notes)

source_schema.method: The documented field set of the Realtime RecognitionStarted message was read from the page above: message, orchestrator_version, id and language_pack_info (language_description, word_delimiter, writing_direction, itn, adapted). The documented-optional channel_ids array is omitted because this fixture represents a single-channel session. No vendor example payload, prose or field description was copied — only the documented field names, the literal message-type constant 'RecognitionStarted' and the documented enum member 'left-to-right', which are interface, not expression. Every value is our own fiction. CONFIRMED AGAINST THE LIVE SERVICE 2026-08-15: a session opened against wss://eu2.rt.speechmatics.com/v2 answered StartRecognition with a RecognitionStarted message whose top-level field set was EXACTLY {message, orchestrator_version, id, language_pack_info}, with language_pack_info an object nesting word_delimiter — precisely the shape this fixture already had, including the nesting the SDK's own C1 defect depends on. That half of the fixture is therefore no longer documentation-derived: it conforms to what the service actually sends. The confirmation is bounded, and the boundary matters: the observation pins the four top-level names and the nesting of word_delimiter, and does NOT enumerate language_pack_info's remaining members (language_description, writing_direction, itn, adapted), which stay documentation-derived. The controlled comparison that makes the observation meaningful is the auth one recorded on the same day — the same credential sent as ?jwt= was answered with an upgrade and then close 4001 not_authorised, so a session reaching RecognitionStarted at all is attributable to the credential channel and not to a service that accepts anything. The frame's VALUES remain our own fiction — the nil-GUID session id and the '0.0.0-fixture' orchestrator version were not observed and are not vendor output — so the class stays `synthetic`; nothing of the vendor's response was stored.

notes: The session-greeting control frame, sent by the fake in answer to the client's StartRecognition message rather than on a timer, which is the sequencing the real service uses and the sequencing the fake already had. It replaces a two-field placeholder and carries the nested language_pack_info object the documentation describes, so the recognizer's lifecycle filter is now exercised against a frame with a genuinely different shape. Its word_delimiter field is worth a reader's attention: Speechmatics publishes the delimiter to join tokens with, and the SDK ignores it and hard-codes a single space — see the add-transcript sidecar for what that costs. WHY THIS IS DOCUMENTATION-DERIVED RATHER THAN CAPTURED, and it is NOT a terms problem: Speechmatics STT is recorded as permitted in section 7 of the protocol guide, so the terms would have permitted a capture; the reason there is no capture is that NO CAPTURE RUN HAS BEEN MADE — not that no credential exists. As of 2026-08-18 a working credential for this surface does exist and a live session has streamed audio through it and elicited real transcript frames (provider-wire-protocol-conformance sections 4.1 and 4.7). Those frames were read to settle the assembly questions in section 4.7 and were NOT stored: nothing of the vendor's output is committed to this tree, which is why this file's class stays 'synthetic'. What the live session did confirm is the SHAPE this fixture claims — the documented field set, the nesting of word_delimiter inside language_pack_info, the presence of metadata.transcript on both AddTranscript and AddPartialTranscript, and a punctuation result carrying attaches_to 'previous' — all observed exactly as documented. So the does-the-vendor-honour-its-own-docs half of the ADR-0041 D4 gap is now closed for this field set, while the half a capture would close (the vendor's own values, on a dated day) is not. Neither the terms nor a missing credential stands in the way any longer: a real capture is a demonstrably reachable upgrade path rather than a merely cleared one. What this artifact is worth, stated plainly: a documented schema is what the vendor says it sends, not what it sent on any given day, and this route cannot close the does-the-vendor-honour-its-own-docs half of the ADR-0041 D4 gap. The page publishes no revision marker, so a silent breaking edit there is indistinguishable from no edit at all. UPGRADED 2026-08-16 (provider-wire-protocol-conformance section 4.6): the field-set half of this fixture is now confirmed rather than assumed, so the does-the-vendor-honour-its-own-docs half of the ADR-0041 D4 gap is closed FOR THE FIELD NAMES AND THEIR NESTING and remains open for everything else — the vendor's values, its behaviour over time, and the nested members the observation did not enumerate. Reaching this frame at all required fixing how the client authenticates: the shipped ?jwt= scheme never opened a session, so before that fix no run of this SDK could have observed the message this fixture stands in for.
